## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sunakhajātaka* (Ja 242) is a short Pali birth story located in the Jātaka collection [Catalog; Fausböll 1879]. The canonical verse opens with the line *Bālo vatāyam sunakho ti* ("Foolish dog") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The framing commentary records that the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana about a dog that was sheltered and fed in the hall by the Ambala tower (*ambalakoṭṭhaka-āsanasālā*), where water-carriers had reared it from birth until it grew stout on donated food [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral registers four modern translations in four languages but lists no direct parallels in other Buddhist canonical corpora [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or higher, confirming the absence of automated alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan witnesses [DharmaNexus].
